tools.name: read_substack_archive
tools.description: Lists a Substack publication's posts, newest first, up to 100 per call: slug, title, subtitle, date, word count, whether it is paywalled (paid posts print only their free preview), and Substack's one-line description. Accepts a handle (aidanjude), a subdomain (aidanjude.substack.com) or a custom dom

tools.name: read_substack_post
tools.description: Returns one post's title, subtitle, date, word count, image count and full text as plain paragraphs (up to 20,000 characters; truncated is true past that). Paid posts return only the free preview Substack shares publicly. Example: {"substack":"aidanjude","slug":"nov-26-pt4"}.

tools.name: find_artist_works
tools.description: Searches the Art Institute of Chicago and the Cleveland Museum of Art open-access collections for works by one artist that the museum itself flags public domain / CC0, and drops everything else. Each work comes back with its museum id (aic:NNN or cma:NNN), title, date, medium, whether it is a line w

tools.name: lay_out_issue
tools.description: Saves an issue (the essays in order, the title, the artist in residence and the works for its plates) and returns a short link to a page where it is already laid out as a stapled 8.5 x 11 in print magazine: cover art, contents, each essay set in print type, a frontispiece, full-page plates on spare

tools.name: price_print_run
tools.description: Prices a print run of a stapled 8.5 x 11 in magazine on 100 lb satin paper: Mixam's print price for that page count and quantity (quoted from Mixam's own calculator, date included), ground shipping to one US address, sales tax, our margin, card fees, the total and the price per copy. tools.name: print_edition_estimate
tools.description: Returns a publication's name, which of its public posts suit a stapled magazine (titled, 600 to 5,000 words), an estimated page count, and the price of one printed copy and of ten. It does not lay out, print or charge for an issue.

tools.name: best_substack_posts_for_print
tools.description: A Substack's posts sorted for print: public, titled newsletter posts between 600 and 5,000 words first, longest first, each with its word count and an estimated page count, and the posts set aside (paid, very short, podcasts, threads) with the reason. Example questions: which of my posts should go i

tools.name: cost_to_print_my_substack
tools.description: What a printed issue of a Substack costs: pages estimated from the chosen posts' word and image counts (or the given page count), then the itemised price (Mixam printing, shipping, tax, Stripe, our margin) at 1, 5, 10 and 25 copies or the number asked. Example questions: how much to print my Substac

tools.name: how_many_pages_will_my_magazine_be
tools.description: The estimated page count of a printed issue: cover, contents, frontispiece, each essay from its words and images, and a back page, rounded up to a multiple of 4, and whether it fits a stapled magazine (80 pages). The issue page gives the exact count once laid out. Example questions: how many pages w

tools.name: price_to_mail_printed_copies
tools.description: Returns the itemised price of printing one copy per reader and mailing each copy by US First-Class: printing, shipping the batch, envelopes, postage and handling. It does not send mail and it does not charge anyone. Reader count is 1 to 100; pass a page count or a Substack to estimate one.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_substack_archive, read_substack_post, find_artist_works, lay_out_issue, is_this_artist_public_domain · Public sink: read_substack_post, price_to_mail_printed_copies · Destructive: price_print_run.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_substack_archive, read_substack_post, find_artist_works, lay_out_issue, is_this_artist_public_domain · Public sink: read_substack_post, price_to_mail_printed_copies · Destructive: price_print_run

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
